   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From:Mr D.H. Phillips, BRIDGEND

Dear Ron and Brian,

First of all thank you for the
prompt attention that you both
have given to my enquiries in
the last few months.

My set-up has been modernised
and now consists of 3 computers:
1) 48k rubber-keyed type. 2) 48k
Spectrum+. 3) 128k Spectrum+.
Three storage systems:1)Disciple
interface and a 3-1/2" P.C. disk
drive (which I believe is compa-
tible with a Spectrum QL system)
2)Interface 1 and 2 microdrives.
3)A tape recorder. Last of all a
Brother M1009 Dual (Parallel/
Serial) type printer.

Now for the questions:-

Is there any way two systems can
be set up in parallel so all the
good points can be utilised?

Set up A)would be a ZX Spectrum+
fitted with the Disciple and the
floppy disc drive driving the
Brother printer.

Set up B) would be the Spectrum
128k+ (which is a dual 48/128k
machine)Interface 1 and the two
microdrives.

Both of the above will be compa-
tible with a cassette recorder
and this the only way I have of
transferring programs between
systems, allbeit a rather slow
method.

As I have a lot of programs on
cartridge and cassette I would
like to be able to utilise the
disc system to swop these all
around and also be able to use
the printer with any system.

Finally, can you supply blank
discs for readers' use?

        Yours sincerely,

            Dave


To Dave Phillips from Brian Gaff

As Brian and Ron have chickened
out on this,it's up to me to
sort it all out!

I assume your problem is
exchanging data between systems.
Both the Disciple and Interface
1 have Net sockets, so it should
be possible to shove data back
and forth that way.

I have no experience with the
Disciple, but if it allows Save
and Load as the IF1 Net does,
then I can see no problems.

The printer could be left
connected to the Disciple, and
its host machine used as a

printer buffer, when you are
using the Microdrive setup. You
would need to write some
software for this though and
adapt existing programs so that
they opened a NET channel.

I would be tempted to suggest
you have the Disciple on the
128K as then you could arrange
at least two of the machines
have an RS232. You could then
get a cheap switch box and share
the printer that way. It would
also mean a serial cable from
IF1 to the 128K RS232 could be
used to exchange data instead of
the Net.                 - B.G.

[We can supply a few discs - if
you send your OUTLET wallet.-BC]

From: Ettrick Thomson, SUFFOLK

Brian doesn't seem to like my
"FOR A=A TO..." (letters, Outlet
41). Fair enough but in my
Spectrum days there were one or
two cases where this was the
tidiest way. Here is an example.
In preparation for a machine
code loader, you want to print
the values of the bytes of some
machine code in groups of 8,each
with a sum-check; there are N
such groups...
 LET A=<address of 1st byte>
 FOR I=1 TO N
 LET S=0: REM sum-check
 FOR A=A TO A+7
 PRINT PEEK A;",";
 LET S=S+PEEK A
 NEXT A : PRINT S : NEXT I

SAM doesn't like this; but, as I
suggested, if you change the 1st
statement to "FOR A=address TO 0
:NEXT A", it works.

          Best Wishes,

         Ettrick Thomson

Brian Cavers to Ettrick Thomson

Sorry, there is some slight mis-
understanding here - possibly
because I only had room on your
previous letter to squeeze in a
one-line comment! I have NO
objection to using FOR A=A TO...
it's just that both in your
previous example and in the one
you give above IT WOULD NOT WORK
CORRECTLY! Try it. Suppose your
initial address is 32768. If you
change your LET A=A TO A+7 to
FOR A=32768 TO 32768+7 or EVEN
if you declare a variable: LET
address=32768 and then use FOR
A=address to address+7, it will
simply keep POKEing addresses
32768 to 32775 which is not what
is intended.

If you search back through some
of my programs in OUTLET you'll
find examples of where I used
say...
FOR N=A TO Z: GO SUB X:
IF... CONDITION THEN NEXT N:STOP
:REM note STOP or GOTO etc. at
the end if it's possible for the
loop to finish!

FOR N=N+1 TO Z: GO SUB Q: NEXT N

         ...where the subsequent
loop takes up where the last one
left off. I think this is a
strength of ZX BASIC missing
from other BASICs and its sad it
has not been implemented in SAM
BASIC. In fact it means I must
now avoid it in ZX BASIC so the
program will convert to SAM with
no problem!

I should just like to affirm
again that the simplest solution
is probably to insert another
variable to temporarily hold the
value and then pass it to the
new loop.To take your example...

 LET A=address
 FOR I=1 TO N
 LET S=0
 LET TEMP=A
 FOR A=TEMP TO TEMP+7
 ETC...
 NEXT A
 NEXT I

I hope that clarifies it a bit!

                       - Brian

From: G.A. Matthews, ESSEX

Re: the letter in Issue 41, I am
unlucky enough to have had an
MGT Lifetime drive for some
time! Indeed I have had it in
bits several times. It uses
virtually the same plug-in drive
made by Citizen as the SAM
Coupe. It bumps and grinds just
like the one in my Coupe.It will
only work with my niece's Plus 3
in 48k mode; God knows why - I
don't. It will only format to
178k one side on the 3.5" disks.
I think the Plus 3 disk control
chip will only handle that. It
formats to 780k double-sided on
my Disciple. I have also had it
working with an ATARI ST where
it formatted using FCOPY3 to
820k.

At least the dip switches are
very accessible, being at the
rear next to the on-off switch.
The connection cable at the
drive end looks like a standard
printer connector. The other end
differs depending on what you
are connecting it to, i.e., you
need a different cable for the
Plus 3 than the Disciple. These
cost `12 a throw.

The handbook, if you can call it
that, says you must have an MGT
gadget called a Fixer to get it
to work with the Plus 3 or Plus
2A. I got a strange verroboard
thing from a gadget-mad friend
which fell apart a month later
but, with the way she treats it,
I'm surprised anything survives!

According to the said handbook,
using Locomotive's CP/M, format
capacity can be increased to
706k.
             Yours,

          Barking Mad,

          G.A. Matthews




Thanks George. A special format
routine is needed to format a
DD/DS 3.5" drive external to the
Plus 3.We had one in an OUTLET a
few months ago which failed to
work correctly but we are trying
to contact the author for a true
working copy...  - Brian Cavers

>PETER WRIGHT FROM BRIAN CAVERS
My view is that purchasing a 128
Spectrum will offer you very
little more at this stage of the
Spectrum's lifetime than the 48K
unless you have some specific
aim and money is not crucial.
There has never been a large
amount of software taking
advantage of the extra Spectrum
memory or improved sound.

I would recommend you purchase a
Plus D interface and drive. It
gives 780K on a disk that costs
far less than a pound whereas
the 3" discs used by the +3 are
between `2 to `3 and only give
about half that AND it is split
between two sides of the disc
requiring you to physically turn
over the disc.

Furthermore, if you eventually
get a SAM you will be able to
transfer some of the software
directly from the +D disc.

The "ERASE ALL" option usually
says something like "ERASE ALL
BASIC EXCEPT..".It does not mean
ERASE the program on the disc -
but from MEMORY leaving just one
small part you can MERGE in, and
use within, your own programs.
Perhaps I should re-word it as
EXTRACT... to avoid confusion.

                - Brian Cavers

in the SCREEN options, you will
get the picture!        - Brian

From: J.E. Hutchings, NUNEATON


I am now trying to transfer my
serious software to SAM. Tasword
was no problem with LERM but
MASTERFILE is. I use MASTERFILE
a great deal and find it a very
good program. Having contacted
Transform and established that
there is no chance of a SAM
version, I tried SD's Specmaker
which converted VU-CALC but not
MASTERFILE. Therefore,LERM would
seem to be the only possibility
- a task I haven't been able to
accomplish. Can anyone help?

        Yours sincerely,

         J.E. Hutchings

Brian Cavers to J.E. Hutchings

Yes. I have just transferred my
MASTERFILE using Dave Stewart's
brilliant EMUTILITY (OUTLET 34).
It works fine and you can update
the data and resave to disc too.
Note that my MASTERFILE is the
48K version. I think there is a
128K version which may or may
not transfer by this means. Here
is what you do...

If you just want a blank version
of MASTERFILE (i.e., you have no
existing records you want to
transfer)just use STAGE 2 on the
next page and use your original
MASTERFILE tape.If you only have
a disc version or have records
to transfer, start at STAGE 1...

STAGE 1: ON THE SPECTRUM:

Load MASTERFILE (and records if
any). Enter USER BASIC (see the
manual). Line 4035 should be...

4035 LOAD ""CODE:GO TO 1

          ...but if not alter it
or type it in again and ENTER.

SAVE to tape using...

SAVE "MF" LINE 4035

SAVE "MFCODE"CODE 57037,8499

(check your MF manual. It's
possible your code is a slightly
different version.)

STAGE 2: ON THE SAM COUPE:

LOAD EMUTILITY. Press G to enter
Spectrum mode.It should reset so
you are in 48K BASIC. Enter:

CLEAR 57036: LOAD ""

Now play the tape saved at STAGE
1 above or your original MF tape
and go and have a coffee. The
coffee is most important else it
doesn't work properly I find.

When you come back you should
see the MASTERFILE menu on your
SAM screen. Lightly baste the
turkey... Sorry - wrong piece of
paper. Lightly press the BREAK
button at the back right of the
SAM and select the SAVE option
to save to disk.

Whenever you use MASTERFILE you
must first load EMUTILITY but it
is possible to set it all up to
load automatically by modifying
the EMUTILITY BASIC and renaming
it MASTERFILE. If anyone needs
any help with that let me know.
It should also be possible to do
a printer option but this needs
a code routine to switch back
from Spectrum mode to SAM.

When you add new data and wish
to resave to disc do NOT use the
save option on the MASTERFILE
menu.ALWAYS use the BREAK button
and save at the EMUTILITY menu.

Let me know how you get on.

                        - Brian

From: David Smith, WOLVERHAMPTON

Dear Sir,

I just read your mag. No.38 and
found it most enjoyable being
new to disc drives.  I am still
learning.

What I would like to know is how
to use the +D Ram and the
execute command. I have tried to
use the execute command as the
manual shows but all I get is
the keyboard locked out .

What am I doing wrong?  HELP!

        Yours faithfully,

          DAVID SMITH

To David Smith From Brian Cavers

I'd never tried EXECUTE before
but I did a couple of tests on
my Disciple without problems. I
assume the +D works in the same
way.

My first thoughts are of three
possible areas that may give
rise to your troubles.A hardware
fault; misuse of the EXECUTE
command itself or something in
your own code that doesn't work.

A hardware fault is probably the
least likely and should only be
considered if all else fails. In
such a case,set up your code and
BASIC and send it to me to test
on my set-up.

Now, to eliminate a problem with
your own code, POKE 201 into
memory somewhere and just save
that as the first address in an
EXECUTE command. It should just
come up O.K. when re-loaded by a
direct command. If so then there
must be something odd about your
own machine code program.If not,
double-check the instruction in
the +D manual. The Disciple is
SAVE D1 "FILENAME" X, ADDRESS

I notice there is a comma BEFORE
the X in my manual and this is
wrong - I assume that is not the
problem? To reload use LOAD P5
(or whatever the directory No.)
or LOAD D1 "FILENAME" X. It's
difficult to see how there could
be room for error there!

Which leaves your own code. Are
you certain your own code runs
O.K. normally - i.e., if called
with USR, and that it is not
longer than 510 bytes? Are you
CERTAIN it will run at a start
address of 7126 decimal(may be
different on the +D) or that it
will run at any address? Are you
CERTAIN it makes no CALLS to the
Spectrum ROM, e.g. RST 16 to
PRINT or, if it does, you use
the indirect method outlined in
the manual?

Let me know if you still cannot
solve the problem.

Does anyone else have any other
suggestions?
                     - Brian.

From Stephen Wilson, AYRSHIRE
I'm having a bit of trouble with
linking my Amiga & SAM together
using the RS232 ports.I heard in
Computer Shopper,somebody did an
Amiga-Speccy link using the same
method but they linked TXd-TXd,
RXd-RXd, SAM DTR-AMIGA RTS? That
can't be right!?? You can't link
output-output. My lead is...

         SAM       AMIGA
         Rxd        TXD
         TXD        RXD
         CTS        RTS
       SYS GND    SYS GND
            ...but still no data
when I use the comms prog you
get with the comms interface:Use
OPEN #S;"b":INPUT #6;a$:PRINT a$
- any knowledge on the subject?
               - Stephen Wilson

> Stephen Wilson from Brian Gaff


Yes, your wiring sounds right to
me; I have not got an Amiga
though! The problems may be due
to handshaking. Many terminals
drive the serial port in odd
ways. They expect to be talking
to Hayes modems!


Assuming that the lead is OK,
and the baud rate, parity, data
bits and stop bits all agree at
either end, it is more than
likely that the terminal program
you are using on the Amiga needs
configuring differently. Try
fiddling with options like Hard-
ware handshaking, and XON/XOFF.

On the SAM side,there is a prob-
lem in the software supplied but
it only affects INKEY$ and is
not that serious. It is indeed
possible to get a SAM on line
from Basic,albeit in a crude way
so the port is a huge improve-
ment over the Sinclair RS232s!

                        - B.G.

From: Simon Greenfield, LINCOLN.

Dear Ron & Brian,

First of all may I just wish you
both a happy New Year and all
the best for the next four.

Right, down to business. I noted
my letter in Outlet 40 and had
to reply to Brian's response as
to "where have I been" concern-
ing the Rom 3 issue. There would
appear to be some confusion here
over this, let me explain. I up-
graded my Rom/Dos back in August
as I initially purchased my SAM
in Dec 89'.  Therefore I had Rom
1 ie: the crap one.  After MGT

with Bob Brenchley who told me

Rom/Dos upgrades. At the same

2.0' yet I have read people
talking about having Rom 3 in
their possession. A program in
either issue(s) 2 or 3 of SAM
SUPPLEMENT says "I have Rom 3
fitted". How can we have jumped
from Rom 1 to 3 missing 2 in the
process? Please can you throw
some light on this as I appear
to have made like a mushroom and
been left in the dark, in other
words I'm @#$%ing confused.

I would like to thank Mr. Talbot
for the disk he sent me for
converting FLASH to do colour

dumps from within the program
using Dave Tonks' excellent pro-
gram FLASHMOD(see SAM SUPPLEMENT
3). Thanks Darren,your free game
SAM puzzle was also brill.

I've commented before on the
excellent screens that keep
appearing in Demopix and thought
that Outlet could use the screen
of the Coupe that appeared in
Issue 40 as a loading screen for
future issues of the SAM Outlet,

screens or are they all convert-
ed from the ST and if so, what's
the program and is it available

Brian Cavers to Simon Greenfield



Thanks, Simon.

If you type PRINT PEEK 15/10 you
will see the ROM version printed
up on screen. There was a ROM 2
which was only issued to a few
users just before MGT went bust.
The"ROM 2" message with your ROM
3 upgrade was presumably just
not updated. If MGT already had
thousands of leaflets printed
and were then struggling with
limited resources of both time
and money to get SAM back on the
rails they probably just let it
go as a temporary anomaly.

Many of the screens in DEMOPIX
are transferred from my ST using
an MGT program. I've never put
it in OUTLET as I believed it to
be copyright although I recently
saw it on a public domain disc
so presumably it is now free to
use. I also use another program
of my own to adjust the size of
the screens because they are not
quite the same.

Other screens in DEMOPIX are off
public domain discs, some sent
in by readers and some I do
myself. The SAM COUPE screen was
one of my efforts. However, I do
like a different screen for the
title page each month. If anyone
else has any SAM (or Spectrum)
screens (their own or PD) please
share them with us all! - Brian

From: Gordon F. Norman, FIFE

My SAM was returned to MGT twice
with the same fault, i.e., on
engaging a disk for initial time
in a session, and "F9ing", the
drive runs 'ad infinitum' to no
purpose.  Occasionally during a
session the same thing happens.

My "Cure" was to switch the
mains "off,on,off" whilst fault
on - MGT frowned on this method!
Lately, I've found that pressing
escape, delete, escape, delete,
before F9 usually cures it!  Any
assistance would be appreciated.

Ref: Auto menu -Outlet No.34.
I can work BASIC files o.k but
other file types result in
"loading procedure fault error".

Please could you explain how, or
is it just not possible, to LOAD
the other types of files. ie.
CODE,$ and numerical arrays etc.
for re-use.

Is it possible to SAVE the main
menus from several "Outlet"
discs in file for perusal, to
reduce search times for items,
using "Auto menu" facility, to
form a catalogue? ie. one
"Outlet" index in each file.

Good luck with OUTLET, a useful
and informative magazine.

        Yours faithfully,

        Gordon F. Norman

Brian Cavers to Gordon Norman

We also have 3 separate drives
afflicted with the same problem.
I'm beginning to suspect that
the connections at the back are
not as solid as they should be.
True, the screws underneath hold
the drives firmly but I feel the
drives are not gripped by the
back socket strongly enough for
my liking. I'm trying some tests
over the next few months and
will report any conclusions.

Yes, AUTOmenu can load any file
but what it will do when loaded
will depend on the file. For
example, this file you are now
reading is text saved as a code
file called "LETTERS2.#" or

"LETTERS3.#" but you will not be
able to read the text without a
program to display the text. If
you enter SAM BASIC and enter
DIR 1 you will see the filenames
with a file number on the left -
suppose "LETTERS2.#" is No.30.
If you enter LOAD 30 the text
will load into the SAM's memory
and just sit there. It cannot do
anything of itself. It needs a
program to display it. Further-
more, our textfiles, Tasword
files, and many other code files
will occupy the SAME place in
memory that AUTOmenu occupies so
will cause a "crash" - that is,
the computer will reset or just
"lock up" the keyboard because
two programs have been jumbled
together.

AUTOmenu should be able to load
SCREEN$ and some auto-running
code files o.k.; I would imagine
you could load the DUMP code for
example. However, many files you
see in a disc directory are not
intended to be loaded other than
into a specific program.

The same would also be true of
my CATLOADER (OUTLET 33) but,for
the reasons given, I decided it
was just not worth including an
option to load other than BASIC
and SCREEN$(I may change my mind
on any future version).

Regarding your wish for a group
of OUTLET menus for reference, I
am pleased to report that we
should soon have an index which
you can use.          - Brian.

Да. Я как раз перенес свой MASTERFILE с помощью великолепной EMUTILITY от Dave Stewart (OUTLET 34). Все работает отлично, к тому же можно обновлять данные и сохранять обратно на диск. Учтите, что у меня 48K-версия MASTERFILE. Кажется, существует и 128K-версия, которая может перенестись этим способом, а может и нет. Вот что нужно сделать...

Если вам нужна чистая версия MASTERFILE (то есть нет существующих записей для переноса), просто переходите к ШАГУ 2 ниже и используйте свою оригинальную кассету MASTERFILE. Если же у вас только дисковая версия или нужно перенести записи, начните с ШАГА 1...

**ШАГ 1: НА SPECTRUM:**

Загрузите MASTERFILE (и данные, если есть). Войдите в USER BASIC (см. руководство). Строка 4035 должна выглядеть так:

```text
4035 LOAD ""CODE:GO TO 1
```

...но если это не так, измените её или введите заново и нажмите ENTER.

Сохраните на ленту с помощью:

```text
SAVE "MF" LINE 4035
SAVE "MFCODE"CODE 57037,8499
```

(сверьтесь с инструкцией к вашему MF. Возможно, у вашей версии кодовый блок немного отличается.)

**ШАГ 2: НА SAM COUPE:**

Загрузите EMUTILITY. Нажмите G для входа в режим Spectrum. Должен произойти сброс, и вы окажетесь в 48K BASIC. Введите:

```text
CLEAR 57036: LOAD ""
```

Теперь запустите ленту, сохраненную на ШАГЕ 1, или вашу оригинальную кассету MF и идите пить кофе. Кофе — это самое главное, без него, как я заметил, ничего толком не работает.

Когда вы вернетесь, на экране SAM должно появиться меню MASTERFILE. Слегка полейте индейку соком... Извините — не та бумажка. Слегка нажмите кнопку BREAK сзади справа на SAM и выберите опцию SAVE, чтобы сохранить всё на диск.

Каждый раз при использовании MASTERFILE вам придется сначала загружать EMUTILITY, однако можно настроить автоматическую загрузку, если модифицировать BASIC-загрузчик EMUTILITY и переименовать его в MASTERFILE. Если кому-то нужна с этим помощь, дайте знать. Также должна быть возможность прикрутить вывод на принтер, но для этого потребуется кодовая процедура для переключения из режима Spectrum обратно в SAM.

Когда вы добавляете новые данные и хотите сохранить их на диск, НЕ используйте пункт сохранения в меню MASTERFILE. ВСЕГДА нажимайте кнопку BREAK и сохраняйте через меню EMUTILITY.

Дайте знать, как пойдут дела.  
— Brian

### Brian Cavers отвечает Gordon Norman

У нас есть 3 отдельных дисковода с точно такой же проблемой. Я начинаю подозревать, что контакты на задней панели не настолько надежны, как следовало бы. Да, винты снизу держат дисководы крепко, но мне кажется, что задний разъем фиксирует дисководы не так плотно, как хотелось бы. В ближайшие несколько месяцев я проведу кое-какие тесты и сообщу о выводах.

Да, AUTOmenu может загрузить любой файл, но то, что произойдет после загрузки, зависит от самого файла. Например, тот файл, который вы сейчас читаете, представляет собой текст, сохраненный как кодовый файл с именем "LETTERS2.#" или "LETTERS3.#", но вы не сможете прочитать этот текст без программы для его отображения. Если вы выйдете в SAM BASIC и введете DIR 1, то увидите имена файлов с номерами слева — предположим, "LETTERS2.#" идет под номером 30. Если вы введете LOAD 30, текст загрузится в память SAM и будет просто там лежать. Сам по себе он ничего сделать не может. Ему нужна программа для отображения. Кроме того, наши текстовые файлы, файлы Tasword и многие другие кодовые файлы займут то же самое место в памяти, которое занимает AUTOmenu, что приведет к сбою («crash») — то есть компьютер сбросится или просто зависнет клавиатура из-за того, что две программы перемешаются друг с другом.

AUTOmenu должно без проблем загружать SCREEN$ и некоторые автоматически запускаемые файлы машинного кода; полагаю, вы могли бы загрузить, например, код DUMP. Однако многие файлы, которые вы видите в каталоге диска, вовсе не предназначены для загрузки куда-либо, кроме конкретной программы.

То же самое относится и к моему CATLOADER (OUTLET 33), но по указанным причинам я решил, что просто не стоит добавлять возможность загрузки чего-либо, кроме BASIC и SCREEN$ (возможно, я изменю свое решение в будущей версии).

Что касается вашего пожелания собрать меню OUTLET воедино для удобства поиска, я рад сообщить, что вскоре у нас появится индекс, которым вы сможете воспользоваться. — Brian.
